concept.name: Price improvement
concept.definition: Execution of an order at a better price than the best displayed quote at the time: for a buy, below the national best offer; for a sell, above the national best bid. It is a formal execution-quality metric in Reg NMS reporting and a headline benefit claimed for retail order routing to wholesalers.
concept.intuition: The screen said the offer was $20.00 but you got filled at $19.995 - that half cent per share is price improvement.
concept.mechanics: Improvement comes from liquidity priced inside the spread: midpoint matches, hidden orders, exchange retail price improvement programs with sub-penny increments, and wholesalers internalizing retail flow at fractional-penny better prices. Reg NMS Rule 600 defines 'executed with price improvement' relative to the NBBO for Rule 605 reporting.
concept.formula: For a buy: improvement per share = national best offer - execution price; for a sell: execution price - national best bid.
concept.failure_modes: Reported improvement is benchmark-sensitive: fractions of a cent vs. NBBO can coincide with worse outcomes vs. the midpoint or post-receipt prices, and aggregate statistics can flatter wholesalers. Size is limited - improvement typically applies to small retail orders, not institutional blocks.
concept.misconceptions: Price improvement is not a guarantee attached to any order type - it is an opportunistic outcome. And 'improved vs. NBBO' does not necessarily mean best available outcome across all venues.
concept.example: A 200-share market buy with the NBBO at $10.00 x $10.02 executes at $10.01 through a wholesaler: one cent per share of price improvement, disclosed in the venue's Rule 605 statistics.
